private_notes.observations: No prior rates or hour allocations are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate markup to establish a baseline. Compare our rate and allocated hours with the published panel rates after the quarter, then adjust to balance margin against volume.

private_notes.observations: No historical rates or allocations are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate above cost, then adjust based on observed panel rates and our allocated hours while prioritizing long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: No prior rates or hour allocations are available. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that provides a meaningful margin, then use published panel rates and our allocated hours to adjust in future quarters.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned about $74,690. Birchwood Hale charged $325, while Calder Rowe also charged $350. One quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to price.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate increase to improve margin while monitoring its effect on allocated hours. Reassess against the next published rate card and profit results.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $325 rate was $25 below both competitors’ $350 rates and yielded 821 allocated hours and approximately $102,619 in profit. We have only one quarter of allocation data, so demand sensitivity is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate moderately to improve margin while remaining below the other firms’ last published rates. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned approximately $74,690. The other firms charged $350 and $325; one quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly allocation responds to price.
private_notes.plan: Hold the rate steady to preserve margin and establish a second-quarter baseline. Reassess after seeing the next rate card and our allocated hours.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $350 in Q1 to $365 in Q2 coincided with hours falling from 498 to 445 and profit declining slightly. Birchwood raised its rate from $325 to $340; Calder remained at $350. The allocation effect of our rate change cannot be isolated from other factors.
private_notes.plan: Test a rate just below Birchwood's latest published rate to seek more hours while retaining a substantial margin. Compare the resulting profit and allocation with prior quarters before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $325 to $340 left quarterly profit nearly unchanged at about $102,700, while allocated hours fell from 821 to 734. Our $340 rate remained below both competitors’ published Q2 rates.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340: the observed gain in margin nearly offset the loss of hours, suggesting we are near a profit-maximizing rate. Reassess after seeing Q3 allocation and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $350, allocated hours rose from 498 in Q1 to 601 in Q2 while both other panel firms raised rates by $15. This suggests room for a modest increase, though Meridian's allocation formula remains unknown.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate by $15 to test demand while maintaining a $165 margin per hour. Monitor next quarter's allocated hours and rate card before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Q3's $335 rate, below both rivals, produced 734 hours and approximately $99,040 profit—the strongest quarterly result so far. Higher rates in Q1 and Q2 produced fewer hours and less profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $335 to preserve the demonstrated allocation advantage. Reassess after seeing Q4 hours and the next published rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $340, profit fell from $102,697 in Q2 to $92,934 in Q3 as allocated hours dropped from 734 to 664; Arden & Cole cut its rate to $335 in Q3. Our $325 rate produced $102,619 profit in Q1.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to regain a price advantage over Arden & Cole and seek more hours. Reassess once Q4 hours and the panel rate card are available.

private_notes.observations: At $365 in Q3, allocated hours fell to 403 as both rivals priced at $335–$340, reducing quarterly profit to $66,433. At $350, prior quarterly profits were $74,690 and $90,087.
private_notes.plan: Set $335 to match the lowest recent rival rate and test whether increased hours outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after seeing the Q4 allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $335, allocated hours fell from 734 in Q3 to 572 in Q4 as Birchwood lowered its rate to $325 and Calder lowered its rate to $335. Q4 profit was $77,277, below Q3's $99,040.
private_notes.plan: Match Birchwood's latest $325 rate to improve our competitive position while retaining a $125 margin per hour. Reassess allocation and competitors' responses next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q4, we earned $87,395 on 699 hours, despite a rate advantage over both firms. Our highest quarterly profit was about $102,700 at $340 in Q2. The recent decline in hours makes the benefit of further discounting uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest increase to $345 to improve margin while monitoring allocated hours and the next published rate card. Reassess whether the higher margin offsets any lost volume.

private_notes.observations: Q4's $335 rate produced 572 hours and approximately $77,277 profit. Raising the rate to $365 in Q3 coincided with substantially fewer hours and lower profit, though rival rates also changed. The four quarters do not establish a reliable allocation formula.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $335 for another quarter. This preserves a solid margin while remaining competitive with recent panel rates. Reassess after observing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q5, we received 737 hours and earned about $92,000. At $335 in Q3, we received 734 hours and earned about $99,000, though competing rates differed. Lower rates have generally increased our allocation.
private_notes.plan: Raise to $335 to capture a higher margin while remaining competitive with the latest published panel rates. Reassess the hours allocated and the next rate card before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: At $345 in Q5, allocated hours fell to 494 and profit to $71,674, while competing rates were $325 and $335. Q4's $325 rate produced 699 hours and $87,395 profit, although demand may also have changed between quarters.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate to $325 to regain volume and test whether the additional hours outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after seeing Q6 allocation and the published rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $335 in Q4–Q5, allocated hours rose from 572 to 604 and quarterly profit rose from $77,277 to $81,505. Q5 competing rates were $325 and $345. Past results suggest that raising our rate when a competitor is cheaper may reduce hours substantially.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $335 to preserve the recent combination of volume and margin. Reassess after Q6 using our allocation and the published rate card; avoid reacting to competitor rates alone.

private_notes.observations: At $335 against Birchwood's $325 and Calder's $335, we received 572 hours in both Q4 and Q6, earning about $77,277 each time. At $325 in Q5, we received 737 hours, though competitors' rates were higher that quarter. The evidence favors testing a modest reduction, but does not isolate its effect from competitors' rates.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to improve our relative price while preserving a $125 hourly margin. Compare allocated hours and profit with the repeated $335 outcomes, and reassess after the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325 against two $335 competitors, we received 699 hours and earned $87,395 in both Q4 and Q6. Raising our rate to $345 while competitors charged $325 and $335 reduced profit to $71,674. The most recent rate cut restored volume, but not enough to match Q1–Q2 profits when competitors charged more.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $315. The lower rate may gain enough hours to offset the $10 reduction in margin; compare the resulting profit with the repeatable $325 benchmark before making further changes.

private_notes.observations: At $335, quarterly profit has been $77,277–$81,505 across Q4–Q6. The identical Q4 and Q6 rate cards produced identical allocations of 572 hours. Raising to $365 in Q3 yielded only $66,433.
private_notes.plan: Hold $335 to maintain a favorable balance of margin and allocated hours. Reassess if the panel rate card or our hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $325, profit was $92,177 in Q5 and $76,610 in Q7. The lower Q7 result coincided with Birchwood cutting its rate to $315. The two $335 quarters with identical rival rates each produced $77,277.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $325 rate to retain a $125 hourly margin while remaining competitive. Reassess if Birchwood's $315 rate persists or allocated hours fall further.

private_notes.observations: The $315 test produced approximately $86,086 in Q7 profit, below the $87,395 earned at $325 in each of Q4 and Q6. Raising the rate to $345 in Q5 reduced profit substantially when competing rates were lower.
private_notes.plan: Return to the repeatable $325 benchmark. Monitor the next allocation and panel rate card before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $335, allocated hours fell from 572 in Q6 to 502 in Q7 as both competing firms cut their rates by $10. At Q7 volume, a $325 rate would need about 543 hours to outperform $335.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate by $10 to seek enough additional hours to offset the lower margin. Reassess after observing the allocation and next rate card; avoid a larger cut without evidence it would improve profit.

private_notes.observations: At $325, recent quarterly profit has been about $77,000. At $335 with a competing rate of $325, profit was also about $77,000. A rate between them may improve the margin without sacrificing many hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $330 as a modest increase and compare the resulting hours and profit with recent quarters before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $325, profit was about $87,395 when both competitors charged $335, but fell to $77,564 when both charged $325 in Q8. Charging $315 in Q7 yielded $86,086, though competitors’ rates were higher than in Q8.
private_notes.plan: Set $315 to compete for hours while retaining a $115 hourly margin. Reassess after seeing the Q9 allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q8, we received 621 hours and earned $77,564 with both other firms also at $325. The Q7 $335 rate earned $67,741 when competitors were at $325 and $315. The evidence does not establish that another cut would increase profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $325 to preserve margin and avoid an untested price cut. Reassess after seeing Q9 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $330 in Q9, hours fell to 540 and profit to $70,239 while rival rates were $315 and $325. Recent $325 quarters produced higher profits, though rival rates varied. Lower relative pricing appears important to retaining hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $320 to improve competitiveness without a large cut in margin. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q7–Q9, and watch whether rival rates continue to fall.

private_notes.observations: At $315 in Q9, we received 729 hours and earned $83,873. Recent results suggest $325 may yield fewer hours and lower profit when competing rates are near $325–$330.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 to preserve a competitive position and a $115 hourly margin. Reassess after the Q10 allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325, Q8–Q9 profit averaged about $76,100. Q9 hours remained strong at 597 despite Birchwood Hale pricing at $315. Past quarters at $335 produced mixed results, and the allocation response to a small rate change remains uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $325 to retain a competitive position without sacrificing margin through an untested cut. Reassess if panel rates or allocated hours shift materially.

private_notes.observations: Q10's $320 rate earned approximately $74,722 on 623 hours. Both rivals have recently priced at $325 or below; Birchwood has held at $315 for two quarters. Earlier quarters with a rate below both rivals produced the highest profits, though demand also varies by quarter.
private_notes.plan: Set $310 to undercut the latest published rival rates while retaining a $110 hourly margin. Assess whether the added hours compensate for the lower margin, and adjust if rivals cut further.

private_notes.observations: At $315, quarterly profit has remained around $79k–$86k recently. Competing rates have edged down to $320 and $325, and Q10 hours fell to 688. Raising our rate risks losing hours; cutting it would reduce our margin without clear evidence of a profit gain.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 this quarter. Reassess after observing the next allocation and panel rate card, particularly whether competitors continue lowering rates.

private_notes.observations: At $325, allocated hours declined from 621 in Q8 to 563 in Q10 as competing rates fell. Q10 profit was $70,428. Raising to $335 when competitors were near current levels yielded $67,741 in Q7; a rate cut has not been tested.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $325. The available history does not establish that a lower rate would gain enough hours to offset the lost margin. Monitor the next rate card and allocation before changing course.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q11, we earned $78,265 on 712 hours, slightly more than at $320 in Q10 or $325 in Q8. The latest published rival rates are $315 and $325.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 to preserve the modest price advantage. Reassess if rival rates or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $315, allocated hours fell from 729 in Q9 to 644 in Q11 as Arden & Cole reduced its rate to $310. Recent quarterly profit has declined despite our unchanged rate.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 rather than initiate another price cut. Monitor whether Arden & Cole's lower rate persists and whether our allocated hours stabilize; reassess next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Competitor rates have fallen to $310 and $315. At our unchanged $325 rate, allocated hours declined from 621 in Q8 to 527 in Q11. A modest reduction may recover enough hours to offset its lower margin, though demand also varies between quarters.
private_notes.plan: Set $320 to improve competitiveness without giving up much margin. Compare the resulting hours and profit with recent quarters before considering another change.

private_notes.observations: At $310, Arden & Cole earned approximately $78,000 and $76,000 in Q11–Q12 while remaining below both rivals. Recent higher rates produced less profit when rivals were similarly priced.
private_notes.plan: Maintain the modest price advantage at $310. Reassess after the next rate card and hours allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $315, allocated hours fell from 644 in Q11 to 626 in Q12, while Arden & Cole held at $310 and Calder Rowe cut to $320. Recent quarterly profit has declined.
private_notes.plan: Set $310 to match Arden & Cole and improve our allocation without a steep price cut. Assess whether the additional hours offset the smaller margin before making further changes.

private_notes.observations: At $320 in Q12, we received 567 hours and earned $68,018, up from 527 hours and $65,887 at $325 in Q11 with the same competing rates. Lowering our rate modestly improved profit.
private_notes.plan: Test $310 to see whether additional hours offset the lower margin. Monitor competitors' rates and avoid pursuing volume if it reduces long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $310, allocated hours fell from 692 in Q12 to 632 in Q13 as both other firms lowered their rates to $310. Q13 profit was $69,504. Earlier results suggest higher rates can be profitable when competitors also charge more, but offer less advantage when they match our rate.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than initiate another round of undercutting. Reassess if competitors change rates or allocated hours continue to decline.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q13, we received 632 hours and earned $69,504 while both competitors also charged $310. Recent rate cuts have not consistently improved profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than initiate another price cut. Reassess after seeing whether panel rates and our allocation stabilize.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q13, we earned $69,504 on 632 hours with both competitors also at $310. The recent $320–$325 rates produced similar or lower profits against competitors charging $310–$315.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than cut further for volume or raise the rate while competitors remain at $310. Reassess if panel rates or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $274 in Q14, Arden & Cole received 974 hours and earned $72,056, while both competitors charged $310. The additional hours did not produce a large profit gain over recent quarters at $310.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate partway back toward the competitors’ $310 rates. Test whether $300 retains enough of the volume gained in Q14 to improve profit without sustaining a deep discount.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q14, hours fell to 474 after Arden & Cole cut its rate to $274; Calder Rowe remained at $310. The lower allocation reduced quarterly profit to about $52,000.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than chase Arden’s sharp cut. Watch whether its $274 rate persists and reassess if the allocation loss continues.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q14, hours fell to 474 after Arden cut its rate to $274; Birchwood remained at $310. Previous quarters show that lower rates do not reliably produce enough additional hours to offset the reduced margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 for Q15 rather than chase Arden's sharp cut. Reassess after seeing whether Arden's lower rate persists and how our hours respond.

private_notes.observations: With both competitors at $310, our $300 rate earned $72,129; $274 earned $72,056 despite substantially more hours. A moderate rate between them may improve profit.
private_notes.plan: Test $290 to balance margin and volume. Watch competitors’ next rates and our allocated hours before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: Arden’s $274 rate in Q14 rebounded to $300 in Q15. At our unchanged $310 rate, allocated hours recovered from 474 to 591, though profit remains below earlier quarters.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than encourage further price cuts. Reassess if competitors sustain lower rates or our hours decline again.

private_notes.observations: Arden rebounded from $274 to $300 in Q15, while Birchwood stayed at $310. At our $310 rate, Q15 profit was $64,960 on 591 hours. Recent results suggest raising our rate while competitors remain near $300–$310 could reduce hours enough to offset the higher margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 for Q16. Reassess if competitors raise rates or our allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: With both competitors at $310 for four quarters, our profit was about $69,500 at $310, $72,100 at $300, $73,400 at $290, and $72,100 at $274. The best observed rate in those conditions was $290.
private_notes.plan: Test $285, a modest reduction from the best observed rate, to see whether additional hours outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after the next rate card and allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $310, allocated hours fell to 547 in Q16 as Arden & Cole cut its rate to $290. Calder Rowe remains at $310. Recent results do not establish that a rate cut would increase hours enough to offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 to preserve margin and avoid encouraging further price cuts. Reassess if Arden sustains its lower rate and our hours continue to decline.

private_notes.observations: At $310, Q15–Q16 profit was about $65,000 and $60,000. Arden has cut its rate to $290, but Birchwood remains at $310; the evidence does not establish that matching Arden would increase profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 rather than sacrifice margin to chase uncertain additional hours. Reassess after seeing whether Arden's lower rate persistently reduces our allocation.

private_notes.observations: With both other firms at $310 for five consecutive quarters, our profits were $72,056 at $274, $72,129 at $300, $73,426 at $290, and $73,487 at $285. The $285 rate produced the highest observed profit under the current competitor rates, though the difference from $290 is small.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $285 while competitor rates remain near $310. Reassess if their rates change or allocation shifts materially; avoid deeper discounts without evidence they improve profit.

private_notes.observations: Arden has priced below our $310 rate for four consecutive quarters, and our allocated hours have fallen to 524. A modest rate cut may recover hours, but the available history does not show that it would offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $310 to protect margin and avoid escalating price competition. Reconsider if the decline in allocated hours continues.

private_notes.observations: Arden has cut its rate to $285 while Birchwood remains at $310. Our hours fell from 591 in Q15 to 524 in Q17 at a $310 rate, though quarterly allocations have varied substantially.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310. A cut to $300 would need to lift allocation above roughly 577 hours to beat Q17 profit, and the history does not establish that it would. Monitor whether Arden's lower rate continues to erode our hours.

private_notes.observations: With both competitors at $310 since Q13, $285 produced $73,487 profit in each of Q17 and Q18, slightly above the observed profits at $290, $300, $310, and $274.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $285 while competitor rates and allocations remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: At $310, allocated hours held at 524 in both Q17 and Q18, yielding $57,682 per quarter. Arden held at $285 and Calder at $310.
private_notes.plan: Maintain the $310 rate rather than sacrifice margin to chase Arden's lower price. Reassess if allocated hours decline further or competitors change rates.

private_notes.observations: At $310, our allocation was 524 hours in both Q17 and Q18, yielding $57,682 each quarter. Arden held at $285 and Birchwood at $310. A cut to $300 would require more than 576 hours to improve on that profit.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $310. Recent allocation is stable, and the evidence does not yet show that a $10 cut would gain enough hours to offset the lower margin. Reassess if allocation or rival rates change.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have both held at $310 since Q13. At $285, our allocation and profit have been stable for three quarters at 865 hours and $73,487 per quarter. Nearby tested rates of $290 and $300 produced slightly lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $285 while competitor rates and allocations remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: At $310, allocated hours and quarterly profit have held steady for three quarters at 524 hours and approximately $57,682. Arden has held at $285; Calder has held at $310.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $300 to see whether additional hours outweigh the $10-per-hour margin reduction. Avoid a larger cut that could erode long-run margins; reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $310, with rival rates steady at $285 and $310, our allocation has remained 524 hours for three quarters, yielding about $57,682 per quarter. Past results do not show that a modest rate cut would increase hours enough to offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $310 while the rate card and allocation remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.
